title: cohere --json
description: One line of `cohere --json`: newline-delimited JSON, one object per line, told apart by `kind`. Findings and changed files come first, in any order; the summary is always the last line, so a reader that never sees one knows the run did not finish.

finding.description: One finding: a rule's, or a type error, whose rule is its TypeScript code (TS2322).

path.description: The file, as an absolute path.

rule.description: The rule's name, or the TypeScript code for a type error.

messageId.description: Which of the rule's messages this is. Absent for a type error.

changedFile.description: One file the run rewrote, by fixing or by formatting.

rules.description: The rules whose fixes were applied, for a fixed file.

engineBuild.description: An engine a development cohere built from source before it could check, its sources or the toolchain having changed. Its time is not in the summary's seconds, which are the check's alone. A released cohere builds nothing.

engine.description: The binary built, such as cohere-swift.

key.description: The cache key it was built under, the hash its binary is named by.

ignoreEntry.description: One entry of the root settings' ignorePatterns, or one of cohere's defaults, as this run's discovery counted it.

reason.description: Why the paths are never checked. Absent when none was given.

kind.description: What the paths are. Absent when none was given.

check.description: A check that still reads the paths. Absent when none was named.

file.description: The settings file that wrote the entry, as an absolute path, or the set's name, such as cohere:next, or cohere for one of its defaults.

default.description: One of cohere's defaults, written by no settings file: testdata, which the Go engine and the format walk never enter, and Vendor, which the format walk and the Swift engine never enter. Each holds only there, so a file a tsconfig includes under either is still type-checked and linted, and neither is ever a finding. Absent for an entry a settings file or set wrote.

matched.description: The paths it matched, files and directories it takes whole, among every entry of every directory discovery read before any ignore applied, inside repositories of their own too, and, for an entry the walk found nothing for, at and below the path it names. Zero for an entry a settings file wrote, unless its kind is generated, is a finding, correctness-no-unused-ignore, which fails the run.

ignorePatterns.description: The root settings' ignorePatterns, in a run of several projects, whose summaries are each a project's: the list a run of one carries on its summary. Written once, before the projects' lines.

crash.description: A rule that could not finish a file, or a file nothing could check, because cohere crashed. A bug in cohere, not in the code checked, and it fails the run.

rule.description: The rule that crashed. Absent when the whole file was lost.

cause.description: The panic, as cohere caught it.

summary.description: The run, the last line. `verdict` is what the exit code says; `gaps` is every way the run fell short of checking everything, which a reader deciding whether a passing run can be trusted reads too.

schemaVersion.description: Raised by any change a reader could notice; a new optional field does not raise it.

label.description: The project's path, in a repository with several projects.

error.description: Why the run stopped before it could judge anything, such as a tsconfig that does not load, in the words the human view prints. Present only then, and the verdict is fail.

ignorePatterns.description: The root settings' ignorePatterns, then cohere's defaults, when the run discovered its project. findings counts each dead one, an entry a settings file wrote that matched nothing and whose kind is not generated.

graphSeconds.description: Reading, parsing and binding the program; zero when no graph was built.

formattingSeconds.description: The part of the fix phase's seconds with a format in flight; the fix phase's seconds include it. Absent when no formatter ran.

replayed.description: The run was answered whole from the run cache, and ran no phase.

filesReplayed.description: Files whose findings came from the cache: in a run that computed the rest, those it did not; in a whole replay, every file in scope. Zero only when no file's findings came from the cache.

missReason.description: Why a run the cache could have answered whole was not: no run on record for these arguments, a key and which of its parts moved (the cohere binary, the project root, the arguments, the configuration), or the input that changed. Absent when it was answered whole or reads no cache.

findingsMissReason.description: Why files' findings were not replayed: none on record, a key and which of its parts moved, or how many files had no entry, changed bytes or rules, or were taken without measuring readiness. Absent when every file looked up was replayed.

packageCache.description: What the Go engine's per-package findings cache did in the lint phase, by package. Present only for a Go run that linted, and absent from a replay, which started no engine.

on.description: False under `--no-cache`, and then every count is zero.

hit.description: Packages restored from an entry, with nothing run on them.

written.description: Missed packages that got an entry.

unstorable.description: Missed packages that held a fact no entry can hold.

factsDropped.description: Facts the written entries left out, since nothing outside their package can name their object.

factsSkipped.description: Restored facts skipped, whose object the package's export data does not hold.

waves.description: Times the lint phase analyzed packages, at most two: those whose own inputs moved, then the rest that missed once the early cutoff restored what it could above them.

findings.description: Rule findings, type errors not included.

wouldChange.description: Under `--no-fix`, the files a fix or formatting would rewrite. They fail the run.

cohered.description: The files the run rewrote, fixed or formatted: the `fixed` and `formatted` lines' files, each once.

filesInScope.description: Every file the run was to account for: checked plus cached.

checked.description: The files examined fresh this run.

cached.description: The files the cache answered for.

typesOnly.description: The files an ignorePatterns entry naming "check": "types" matched, beside filesInScope and not in it: type-checked, their type errors reported, and never linted or formatted. Absent when there were none. A file only plain entries match is in no count, since it is never checked at all.

nodes.description: The syntax nodes walked this run, in the checked files.

programFiles.description: The program's size when the run was narrowed to fewer of its files; zero otherwise.

crashedFiles.description: Files nothing could check, because cohere crashed on them. They fail the run.

ruleCrashes.description: Rules that crashed on a file, each leaving its verdict there missing. They fail the run.

path.description: The file, as the engine names it.

rule.description: The rule that crashed. Absent when the whole file was lost.

cause.description: The panic, as cohere caught it.

crashes.description: Each crash crashedFiles and ruleCrashes count, named, so the list is as long as the two together. The same fields as a `crash` line, which a Swift run does not print. Absent when there are none.

rulesSkippingEverything.description: Rules that declined every file they were offered.

nothingToCheck.description: The project had no files to check.

modifiedBuild.description: The binary was built from a modified tree, so no commit reproduces these findings.

unread.description: Files the run could not check for any other reason, as the run said it.

nestedUnread.description: Why the nested repositories could not be read for drift. Their files are never the run's to check, so the run went on. Absent when they were read.

phasesNotRun.description: The check's phases the run has no record of, because it stopped before them, such as a run that formatted and never type-checked or linted. Absent when every phase was reached.

adamicIgnored.description: Adamic .a files the program holds that git's ignore rules leave out of the format walk: type-checked and linted, never formatted. Absent when there are none.

nestedUnchecked.description: Files in the nested repositories the run reads that the formatter could not check, each named in the account. A gap, never the verdict: the nested repository's own run fails on them. Absent when there are none.

missingGenerated.description: Generated files the program asks for that do not exist yet, relative to the project root: an import or reference path in a project file whose target git ignores, such as Next's .next/types before `next typegen`. They fail the run. Absent when there are none.

fixesHeld.description: Lint fixes were held because an input the program was told to load is missing: a generated file, or an import, reference or types entry that resolves to nothing. None was proposed or written, and formatting ran alone. Absent otherwise.

file.description: The file, as the Swift engine names it.

reason.description: Why the engine left it out, in the engine's words, such as "no target of this package compiles it".

uncheckedSwift.description: Swift files a Swift run's engine listed as not checked for a reason other than git ignoring them, Vendor/ or being a package manifest, which today means no target of the package compiles them and they are no standalone script the run checks alone (a file of declarations only, or a script whose imports name two platforms), less those under a Swift project below it that runs on its own. Each is listed, however many share a reason. They fail nothing. Absent when there are none.

package.description: The dependency's package, as the Go engine names it, such as "net".

file.description: The file, as the Go engine names it.

errors.description: The type errors withheld in it.

withheldInDependencyCgo.description: Files of a dependency with cgo files whose type errors a Go run withheld, because no cgo tool ran and the faked package "C" is what they are about, sorted by file. They are a dependency's, not the project's to fix, so they fail nothing. Absent when there are none, as on macOS.

withheldDependencyCgoDeclarations.description: Declarations of dependencies with cgo files that every rule of a Go run was given without their bodies or initial values, because no cgo tool ran. They fail nothing. Absent when there are none, as on macOS.

adamic.description: Adamic readiness: the files whose types are true, with no type error and no cohere:adamic finding before suppression, whatever the project's rules enable. Present only under --adamic-readiness, and then always: a run that asked and could not measure it says so.

reason.description: Why readiness was not measured, in a clause; present only when it was not.

files.description: The files the lint walk measured or tried to.

ready.description: The files with no type error and no cohere:adamic finding.

unmeasured.description: Files a cohere:adamic rule skipped for a missing precondition, or the cache replayed without a count. Never counted ready.

optionsMissing.description: The compiler options Adamic sets that the project's tsconfig leaves off, so the files were measured under weaker options than Adamic's.

failingFilesByRule.description: By cohere:adamic rule, the files it found something in.
